prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: ONE unlabelled 2 by 2 PBR material-channel atlas for a seamless game pavement. Square 4096 x 4096 atlas requested, four exactly square 2048 x 2048 panels, no gutters, gaps, labels or borders. This is a material-data deliverable, not a presentation board or a lit photograph.

Reference images 1 and 2 show Forbidden City alleys. Use ONLY the limestone pavement's pale warm-gray color, substantial rectangular slabs, softly worn chipped edges and fine natural stone grain. Do not copy any scene, viewpoint, architecture, people, cast shadows, sunlight or markings.

All FOUR panels must have the EXACT SAME aligned tile layout, same UV coordinates and same chip positions. Each panel describes the SAME 4 x 4 meter repeatable ground patch. Entirely straight-down orthographic, no perspective. Rectangular pale gray slightly beige limestone slabs in horizontal running-bond courses, with alternating rows shifted half a slab. About eight courses and four slabs per course; slabs roughly 0.6-1.2m wide and 0.4-0.6m high. Slight size and color variation, gently irregular worn rounded bevels, fine mineral grain, tiny edge chips, slight uneven slab heights. Keep the floor useful and walkable, not broken rubble. No moss, dirt piles, weeds, litter, puddles or text.

SEAMLESS PERIODIC MATERIAL: every individual square panel repeats perfectly in both X and Y. Tile joints crossing an edge continue at exactly the same position on the opposite edge, with identical edge values. Use eight complete horizontal courses and an even repeating running-bond cycle. No framing perimeter mortar line, no darker outer border, no bright central patch, no global gradient or vignette. The cropped slab fragments on opposite edges must meet into intact slabs when repeated.

TOP LEFT = ONLY BASE COLOR / ALBEDO: pale limestone with gentle slab-to-slab warm-gray/beige differences and subtle fine grain. Deep joints have intrinsically dark neutral-gray material color, but NO directional shadows, bevel highlights, baked ambient occlusion or lighting. Flat even intrinsic colors, not a shaded render.
TOP RIGHT = ONLY TANGENT NORMAL DATA, OpenGL Y+ convention. Neutral flat centers near RGB(128,128,255). Correct red/green opposing edge slopes indicate soft convex rounded slab bevels descending into recessed mortar and slight natural stone surface unevenness. Violet/blue/cyan/red normal data, NEVER a shaded gray color image. Consistent with bottom-left height and the exact same slab boundaries.
BOTTOM LEFT = ONLY LINEAR GRAYSCALE HEIGHT DATA. Dark recessed mortar/joints, light nearly flat slab tops with modest different height levels. Smooth rounded transitions from bright tops down into dark seams, small chips and subtle stone relief. No light direction, no cast shadows, no photographic shading, no separate specular highlights. White means high, black means low. Not merely a desaturated albedo.
BOTTOM RIGHT = ONLY LINEAR GRAYSCALE ROUGHNESS DATA. Dry matte limestone mostly medium-light gray, slightly rougher mortar and small natural fine texture variation. No lighting, no shaded bevels, no shadows or highlights. Same perfectly aligned geometry. This is roughness, not smoothness or ambient occlusion.

CRITICAL: four equal square panels fill the complete square output exactly; boundaries are at the exact horizontal and vertical center. Do not draw dividing strokes. Each panel is its own complete seamless 4m repeat. No inset preview, no text, no symbols, no labels, no legends. Realistic stone microtexture, no decorative repeated noise or painterly surface.

Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Create ONE entirely new square four-channel stone-pavement MATERIAL ATLAS, requested 4096 x 4096 pixels, divided into FOUR equal square quadrants. No text or separating strokes. Top-left: albedo. Top-right: tangent normal OpenGL Y+. Bottom-left: scalar height. Bottom-right: scalar roughness. Every quadrant describes EXACTLY the same stone positions, shape boundaries, chips and UV coordinates. No photography layout or decorative board.

EXACT GEOMETRY, HIGHEST PRIORITY: in EACH quadrant show EIGHT horizontal courses of rectangular paving slabs, FOUR one-meter slab widths across. Every quadrant represents 4m x 4m. Each slab is about 1m wide by 0.5m tall, twice as wide as tall. Eight rows, not four or five. Four slab widths across, not two or three. Alternate courses shift exactly HALF a slab width. Thus one course has four whole slab widths, the next has three whole slabs and two half-width fragments at the left and right boundaries. Keep this eight-row, four-width running-bond layout IDENTICAL in all four quadrants. Slight natural size irregularity only within this clearly controlled scale, not a change in row or column counts. Narrow recessed seams, naturally chipped and softly rounded slab rims, subtly uneven top levels.

PERIODIC EDGES: each square quadrant is independently seamless and wraps in both directions. Opposite edge fragments and mortar-joint positions meet into complete slabs in a 3x3 repeat. The eight-row stagger cycle ends in the correct phase for the next repeat. No extra framing row, no border stripe, no vignette, no overall gradient. View straight down with zero perspective.

MATERIAL: dry pale warm gray limestone with a very slight beige undertone. Restrained natural fine mineral grain, occasional tiny chips, worn softly rounded edges. Soft modest slab color variation. No moss, weeds, debris, cracks splitting whole slabs, puddles, footprints, inscriptions or large pores. Subtle authentic photographic stone surface, no artificial patterned noise.

TOP LEFT ALBEDO: only intrinsic color, equivalent to an unlit base-color pass. Light gray/beige slab faces and narrow intrinsically darker neutral-gray mortar. No simulated surface lighting whatsoever: no bright bevel edges, no shaded edges, no dark ambient-occlusion halos, no highlights, no sunlight direction. Geometry must be provided by the data maps rather than painted lighting in the albedo.
TOP RIGHT NORMAL: actual blue/purple/cyan tangent-direction data with flat centers near (128,128,255), normalized directions, OpenGL positive Y. Proper opposing red/green slope directions for rounded stone bevels that descend into seams. Same boundaries as the other quadrants. Not a photograph or grayscale render.
BOTTOM LEFT HEIGHT: truly scalar grayscale elevation, not a shaded picture. Bright gently varied flat slab tops, softly rounded descent toward black/dark-gray seam recesses, slight stone relief and chips. Neither highlights nor directional shadows. All eight courses and four widths align with the other maps.
BOTTOM RIGHT ROUGHNESS: true grayscale roughness, dry matte slab faces around 0.65 to 0.8 and rougher mortar around 0.9. Very restrained natural surface variation; NOT a gray photograph, no directional light, no bevel shading, no black shadow lines. Matching UV geometry.

Render only these FOUR flush quadrants, each containing the SAME eight-course four-slab-width layout. Whole canvas opaque. No inset, labels, legends, symbols, perspective, grout border or mockup. Deliver a single atlas.

Generate ONE square 2-by-2 material channel atlas for a seamless limestone pavement. Four equal square panels, no margins or captions. Top-left ALBEDO, top-right OpenGL Y+ NORMAL, bottom-left HEIGHT, bottom-right ROUGHNESS. Every panel must show the identical slab geometry and UV coordinates. Request high-resolution 4096-square output, each map 2048-square.

The single material covers a 4 by 4 meter floor patch. Orthographic top-down. Pale warm gray, very slightly beige limestone, fine grain, gently worn rounded edges, minor chips, small slab-height variation. Large rectangular slabs about 1m wide and 0.5m high, horizontal running bond with half-width offset on alternating courses. Exactly EIGHT COMPLETE courses fit within EACH square map, and about FOUR slab widths across. Do not cut off or shorten the eighth row.

PERIODIC LAYOUT IS THE MAIN REQUIREMENT:
Each map's first row starts at the TOP MORTAR JOINT CENTERLINE; the eighth row ends exactly at the BOTTOM MORTAR JOINT CENTERLINE. Eight complete 0.5m courses, eight equal course heights, total 4m. The top and bottom edge lie in the same neutral mortar material, half a narrow joint at each edge so they join into one ordinary joint when repeated. There is no partial slab row at the top or bottom. Opposite left/right edge fragments use matching stone colors, same heights and identical joint positions, so fragments become complete slabs across repeats. Alternating offset phase repeats correctly after eight courses. No visible rectangular patch boundary in a 3x3 repeat; no decorative perimeter or thicker outer joint. Do not independently change layout between panels.

ALBEDO top-left: only intrinsic light-gray/beige stone color and dark-gray mortar color. Subtle natural slab variation and fine stone grain. NO baked shadows, highlights, sun direction, shaded bevels, ambient occlusion, vignette, or overall gradient. Geometric relief is only in data maps.
NORMAL top-right: blue/purple/cyan tangent vector data, OpenGL Y+. All normals point outward, blue channel above 128 everywhere; flat centers near RGB 128,128,255. Opposed red and green values encode rounded rims descending into joints, subtle grain and small chips. No gray photographic regions or black grout in this map. Same eight complete courses and matching wrap at all edges.
HEIGHT bottom-left: pure scalar grayscale, bright nearly flat slightly varying stone top levels, dark recessed seams, smooth rounded slopes between. No light direction, highlights, cast shadows or grayscale photograph. Same layout; top and bottom pixels are matching dark seam elevation.
ROUGHNESS bottom-right: true scalar gray material roughness, limestone about 0.7 and rougher mortar about 0.9; mild grain. No photographic shading or dark baked shadows. Same layout and matching edges.

No moss, weeds, rubble, litter, water, footprints, figures, architecture, text, labels, grid strokes or inset preview. Four flush equal quadrants only. Real natural stone detail, no painterly or artificial repetitive texture.
